name: Mecca Normal
label: K
lede: A guitar, a voice and a zine that turned into a label: the Vancouver duo Kathleen Hanna says she wouldn't be in a band without.

eras.title: A newspaper office, a borrowed practice room
eras.text: A graphic designer and a poet who met at a Vancouver left-wing paper start a band with one guitar and one voice, then press their own LP and drive it south. Nobody's permission was asked at any point.

years.cap: Jean Smith and David Lester, Vancouver
years.src: Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal - Wikipedia · David Lester (musician) - Wikipedia · Jean Smith (singer) - Wikipedia
years.h: One voice, one guitar, no drummer, no permission
years.p: [[Jean Smith|56b2d08f-076e-4c81-bb6e-9d7cdab65bb1]] and [[David Lester|b6f927cf-2825-4bdb-b4cf-ece5a8da88f0]] meet at a Vancouver newspaper and form Mecca Normal as a duo. It stays a duo, with no drums on record until well into the 1990s.
years.xp:
Lester was working as a graphic designer for the leftist paper Open Road when he met Smith at another local newspaper office. Sources disagree on the start date: K Records and Wikipedia's band page say 1984, while the Smith and Lester biographies on Wikipedia say 1981.

"The main thing is, you didn't ask for permission. You didn't play the capitalist game," Lester told KEXP.

years.src: Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal
years.p: Lester's brother Ken managed the Vancouver hardcore band [[D.O.A.|0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca]] from 1979, which is how a duo with no drummer got its first slot.
years.xp: D.O.A. and the Subhumans were the city's politically engaged punk bands, and Mecca Normal came out of the same scene with far less volume. The show is undated in the sources we found.

years.src: Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal | Trouser Press
years.h: Mecca Normal, on their own label, Smarten Up!
years.p: The debut LP, recorded in a borrowed practice space, comes out on an imprint that grew out of Smith's zine. Trouser Press notes it was made on a cassette 4-track.
years.xp: Smith's zine Smarten Up! became the label for their first record after very few local shows. Trouser Press singles out two songs that became live staples, "Are You Hungry Joe?" and "I Walk Alone." K reissued the album in 1995.

years.src: Normal History Vol. 898: The Art Of David Lester
years.h: Expo 86 evictions, a seven-inch and a Stanley Park benefit
years.p: Mecca Normal contributes a song to a D.O.A. protest seven-inch about evictions in Vancouver's poorest postal code before Expo 86.
years.xp: According to Magnet's history column, a benefit concert in Stanley Park with D.O.A., Pete Seeger and Arlo Guthrie raised $10,000 for people who lost their housing.

years.src: Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal - K Records · Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith
years.h: Black Wedge rolls into Olympia; Calvin Johnson trades a record
years.p: On the Black Wedge tour, [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] swaps [[Beat Happening|449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456]]'s self-titled LP for Mecca Normal's debut at a show in Olympia.
years.xp:
Smith and Lester co-founded Black Wedge in 1986 as a touring bundle of anti-authoritarian poets and minimalist musicians, and borrowed D.O.A.'s tour bus to cover the west coast and the American heartland. The Olympia stop was at GESSCO.

Smith was wary of the yellow Beat Happening album, which shows a cat riding a rocket, and it warped on the bus. Mecca Normal still contributed "Smile Baby" to K's cassette compilation Let's Sea.

eras.title: K Records takes them in
eras.text: Two records for K Records, the second cut in Olympia, and a week in 1991 when a whole generation of girl bands turns out to have been listening.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal - K Records
years.h: Calico Kills the Cat · K Records, KLP004
years.p: First record for K, and a studio better suited to Smith's low register than the debut's cassette 4-track.
years.xp: Trouser Press hears "the seeds of Mecca Normal's future" in it. K reissued it in November 2024.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal, "Water Cuts My Hands"! · Water Cuts My Hands [KLP008], by Mecca Normal
years.h: Water Cuts My Hands, cut in Olympia with Calvin Johnson
years.p: Recorded with Johnson and engineer Patrick Maley, and issued by K and Matador together.
years.xp: K calls it the band's third album. Smith described the title song as an encounter with a street person that leaves a woman wondering why her empathy doesn't override his misogyny. The Village Voice wrote in 1990: "I don't know of any other rock 'n' roll so closely attuned to the realities of women's rage."

years.big: "It makes me wanna cry, I am glad they exist."
q: I wouldn't be in a band if I hadn't heard of Jean.
years.src: Mecca Normal, "Water Cuts My Hands"! · Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal
years.h: What Bikini Kill's singer said about them
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] of [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] in 1991, according to K Records' write-up.
years.xp: In a later interview Hanna is quoted saying she wouldn't be in a band if she hadn't heard of Smith. Smith has said Hanna and Tobi Vail have mentioned Mecca Normal as significant, and that between songs she encouraged women to start bands.

years.cap: International Pop Underground Convention, Olympia, August 1991
years.src: International Pop Underground Convention - Wikipedia · Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith
years.h: Girl Night: Smith plays the Olympia convention's first evening
years.p: [[Jean Smith|56b2d08f-076e-4c81-bb6e-9d7cdab65bb1]] performs on opening night of the six-day International Pop Underground Convention in Olympia, at the showcase for female punk and queercore acts.
years.xp:
The festival ran August 20-25, 1991, centered on the Capitol Theater, with about fifty bands including [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], Bikini Kill and Melvins. Passes were $35 for five days, according to organizer Candice Pedersen.

The opening night was called Love Rock Revolution Girl Style Now, and became a reference point for riot grrrl.

eras.title: Olympia sessions, then Matador and a drummer
eras.text: Three more K records, a compilation of the singles, Smith's first novel, and a move to Matador that finally adds a third musician.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal - K Records
years.p: Johnson and Maley produce again in Olympia, and Lester's playing gets a delicate, melodic side.
years.xp: Trouser Press credits Smith with "increasing control as a vocalist" on the record.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal - K Records
years.p: A K compilation of the band's singles, KLP018, which Trouser Press calls the record that best captures their pull between anger and beauty.
years.xp: Flood Plain (KLP022) arrived the same year, a studio album on which Trouser Press finds the duo "in closer synch than ever."

years.h: Smith publishes her first novel, I Can Hear Me Fine
years.p: Independent presses issue the book in 1993. She follows it with The Ghost of Understanding in 1998.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the second novel incorporates lyrics from several Mecca Normal albums. Smith received Canada Council for the Arts awards in 2000 and 2007.

years.src: Sitting on Snaps - Wikipedia · Mecca Normal | Trouser Press
yt: This is Different, live in San Francisco
years.h: Sitting on Snaps · first record for Matador
years.p: [[Peter Jefferies|20a3f1b5-2c27-491d-a5a6-3f61ae253edd]] of New Zealand plays piano on "Cyclone" and "Vacant Night Sky," and Johnson produces some tracks.
years.xp:
Reviews split hard. Rolling Stone called it "free punk," the Los Angeles Times put Smith's voice in "a space between Grace Slick, Patti Smith and a dental drill," Option called it "highly unlistenable," and Robert Christgau gave it a dud.

The same year Smith formed 2 Foot Flame with Jefferies and Michael Morley of the Dead C, also on Matador.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal - Wikipedia
years.h: The Eagle and the Poodle: a drummer on seven tracks
years.p: Jefferies plays drums on seven of the thirteen songs, the closest Mecca Normal comes to a trio.
years.xp: Trouser Press finds it "surprising how little" the third member changes the band's sound. Who Shot Elvis? followed on Matador in 1997.

eras.title: A lecture tour with amplifiers
eras.text: The band spends the 2000s moving between clubs, classrooms and Kill Rock Stars, and turns the show into a talk.

years.src: Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith · Mecca Normal - Wikipedia
years.h: A tour that plays classrooms, galleries and bookstores
years.p: Mecca Normal builds "How Art & Music Can Change the World," a lecture-performance for rooms that aren't clubs.
years.xp: The 2009 twenty-fifth anniversary tour split its dates between conventional venues and educational spaces, according to Smith's interview with Tamra Lucid. The Family Swan came out on Kill Rock Stars in 2002 and Janis Zeppelin on Smarten Up! in 2003.

years.src: Mecca Normal - Wikipedia · David Lester (musician) - Wikipedia
years.h: The Observer, written out of online dating
years.p: Smith's experiences on dating websites inspire the Kill Rock Stars album.
years.xp: The Globe and Mail named Lester among ten famous Canadians you've never heard of in 2007.

eras.title: Still going, and drawing
eras.text: A new record, a paint-by-subscription series and reissues that finally put the K catalogue online.

years.h: Empathy for the Evil comes out on M'lady's Records
years.p: The 2014 album follows a run of live dates.

years.src: Water Cuts My Hands [KLP008], by Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal, "Water Cuts My Hands"! · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Jean Smith (singer) - Wikipedia · David Lester (musician) - Wikipedia
years.h: K puts Water Cuts My Hands online for the first time
years.p: The album goes digital on June 13, 2025, ahead of a vinyl and digital reissue, with a video that features Smith's painting.
years.xp: Smith has been selling 11x14 inch acrylic portraits through Facebook for $100 each since 2016, aiming to fund a free artist residency. Lester illustrated the 2019 graphic novel 1919: A Graphic History of the Winnipeg General Strike.
